description: Click optimization: 26 clickbait tactics, title formulas, thumbnail design, synergy rules

principles.rule: The reason to watch must be immediately apparent — if it takes longer than 1 second to think of a reason, the title/thumbnail is failing
Titles and thumbnails must BUILD OFF one another, not repeat the same information
principles.implication: Repeating is 'too slow' — viewers scanning competing videos will click something faster. Use both to deliver complementary hooks.

principles.rule: Create thumbnails from SCRATCH — never use frames from the actual video
principles.implication: Separate photographs/images give you full control over composition, mood, and messaging.

principles.rule: The thumbnail should intrigue BEFORE the title is read
principles.implication: Aim for the thumbnail alone to be compelling enough to watch.

principles.rule: The 26 clickbait tactics also serve as criteria for a good video idea
principles.implication: If you cannot apply these tactics to a title/thumbnail, the idea itself may not be viable.

twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Never use frames from the actual video. Represent what happens rather than showing literally.
Exploit the bias that immediate attention goes toward danger.
Unique art styles suggest unique information.
Make the subject pop against the background.
Exploit recognition bias — emojis, celebrities, well-known brands grab attention first.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Suggest the viewer is making a mistake or in danger
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Create fear of missing out on important information.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Focus on the 1-2 most intriguing parts
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Don't describe the whole video, just what makes it interesting.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Thumbnail should intrigue before the title is read
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Standalone visual intrigue.
On mobile, the thumbnail auto-plays after 1 second of not scrolling.
Every color, saturation level, and brightness must be deliberate.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Suggest someone is hiding a secret
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Creates irresistible curiosity.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Help viewers reach their goals or alleviate pain points
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Direct value proposition.
Artistic thumbnails build trust in video quality.
Clarity with uncertainty (I know what's happening but not what happens next) vs confusion (I don't know what's happening). Confusion kills everything.
Thought-provoking questions.
Word choice matters — spend time finding the best synonyms.
Create FOMO with deliberate thumbnail elements.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Create a puzzle with a missing piece
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Works best when the missing piece feels alarming/important.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Challenge beliefs or suggest viewers are misinformed
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: People click to confirm or deny their beliefs.
Use recognized faces/brands for recognition and trust.
Credentials, official documents, military technique, etc.
Viewers want to see problems solved.
Defies expectations.
Shock and fear are most effective — they imply something extraordinary happened.

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Show a situation with an unknown before or after
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Viewer needs to know what happened next (or before).

twenty_six_click_tactics.tactic: Make people think 'there is no freaking way'
twenty_six_click_tactics.description: Do something extraordinary.

thumbnail_spotlight_elements.description: Three elements that draw the most attention in thumbnails

elements.name: expressive_face
elements.description: Humans are naturally drawn to faces. Shock and fear expressions are most effective.

elements.name: familiar_object
elements.description: Recognized brands, logos, items create instant recognition.

elements.name: short_text
elements.description: Keep it brief — never use text for full explanations. 1-3 words max.

thumbnail_storytelling.description: Use visual subtlety to tell a story in the thumbnail

techniques.description: Warm colors (orange/red) = excitement/survival/danger. Cool colors (blue/green) = calm/intelligence. Match target demographic.
Text like 'Day 2' or '41 minutes in' builds excitement and implies a journey.
Body language, environment, and lighting tell a story without words.
Arrows, circles, and borders guide the viewer's eye in a specific order.

title_optimization.description: Title writing rules for maximum CTR
rules: Put the most important and interesting words at the START of the title
Use short, common words with clear meanings
Be dramatic and creative with wording — do not title literally
Title as the 'driving question' rather than describing what happens
Use thesaurus.com and ChatGPT to find better word choices
Questions work well as titles — they create curiosity
Add extra context that the thumbnail can't convey

title_thumbnail_score.description: Score a title/thumbnail pair before committing to production

criteria.name: one_second_scan
criteria.description: Can you understand the reason to watch in under 1 second?

criteria.name: complementary_info
criteria.description: Do title and thumbnail deliver different but complementary hooks?

criteria.name: tactic_count
criteria.description: How many of the 26 tactics does this pair use? Target: 3+

criteria.name: clarity_vs_confusion
criteria.description: Is it clear WHAT is happening but uncertain WHAT happens next?

criteria.name: curiosity_strength
criteria.description: Does it create a strong 'I need to know' feeling?

criteria.name: standalone_thumbnail
criteria.description: Does the thumbnail intrigue even without the title?

criteria.name: word_quality
criteria.description: Are title words short, common, dramatic, and front-loaded?

anti_patterns.mistake: Title and thumbnail repeat the same information
anti_patterns.consequence: Only delivers one reason to watch instead of two. Slower than competitors.
anti_patterns.fix: Make them complementary — each adds a new hook or question.

anti_patterns.consequence: No control over composition, mood, or messaging
anti_patterns.fix: Create thumbnails from separate photographs/images built from scratch.

anti_patterns.mistake: Putting the least interesting words first in the title
anti_patterns.consequence: Titles get truncated on mobile — viewers never see the good part

anti_patterns.mistake: Titling the video literally instead of as a driving question
anti_patterns.consequence: No curiosity generated — viewer feels they already know the content
anti_patterns.fix: Frame the title as the question the viewer will want answered.
